html:
Sungbo's Eredo is a vast system of ditches and earth banks in southwest Nigeria that circles the lands of the Ijebu kingdom around Ijebu-Ode. It runs for about 160 km, with ditches in places some 20 metres deep, and was dug around 800 to 1000.

Eredo is the Yoruba word for such a ditch and rampart. Local tradition says it was built for a noblewoman named Bilikisu Sungbo, whom some people link to the biblical Queen of Sheba; her shrine is a pilgrimage site. Survey and radiocarbon work by the archaeologist Patrick Darling suggested it was dug about a thousand years ago, likely to mark and guard the bounds of a growing kingdom.

It belongs to a wider forest tradition of huge earthworks, like the walls of Benin to the east. Shaded by forest, it is hard to see and has been little studied, but it is on Nigeria's list of hoped-for World Heritage Sites.
